answer: Cross-session behavioral kernel clustering. After the fact, each agent identity accumulates a feature vector from its interaction history; a learned kernel measures similarity between vectors across sessions and clusters near-duplicates. When one operator runs many identities, their shared habits collapse into a tight cluster, flagging the whole set for weight reduction. An attacker must diversify each sock puppet's behavior enough to escape the cluster, paying real compute and dev time per identity. One stray ember of repetition exposes the fable of independence.
